name: Dyeing
overview: Scripture references dyeing primarily in the context of garments and coverings, highlighting both practical and symbolic uses. In Exodus, dyed red rams' skins are commanded for the construction and covering of the tabernacle, signifying a divinely ordained design. Isaiah portrays a figure coming from Edom with dyed garments, emphasizing glory and strength, while Ezekiel describes excessive dyed attire as a symbol of pride and worldly influence among princes. Thus, dyeing in the Bible serves to denote consecration, honor, and sometimes ostentation.
